snippet.description:

The S&P 500 8,700 Target: Goldman Sachs has set a 12-month S&P 500 price target of 8,700 (implying a 14% upside)

snippet.title: Bryant Park Winter Village 2026: Ice Skating & Holiday Market NYC
snippet.description:
Christmas in New York starts here: a night walk through Bank of America Winter Village at Bryant Park, with ice skating under the Midtown skyscrapers, the Holiday Shops market, the Cozy Igloos and the carousel, all lit up.
Plan your Manhattan visit with Atlas: https://atlas.niramind.com/manhattan

What you'll see: the Cozy Igloos and glowing Christmas trees, skaters on the free-admission rink with the Empire State Building and the Midtown towers above, the Silly Puppets kiosk, giant light globes under the trees, rainbow light trees, Pinky Pilots New York and Artisans of New York, hand-blown glass ornaments, the rinkside crowds and The Lodge, the park's giant Christmas tree before its lighting, the ice resurfacing machine smoothing the rink between sessions, and Le Carrousel spinning at night.

CHAPTERS
0:00 Cozy Igloos & Christmas trees
0:31 Ice skating under the Midtown skyline
1:16 Silly Puppets at the Holiday Shops
1:37 Light globes & the Holiday Shops
2:17 Rainbow light trees & Pinky Pilots New York
2:34 Walking the market, glass ornaments & gifts
3:03 Artisans of New York & more kiosks
3:57 Rinkside crowds & The Lodge
4:48 The giant Christmas tree (before the lighting)
5:06 Skaters on The Rink
5:22 Ice resurfacing between sessions
7:48 Skating resumes under the skyscrapers
8:12 Le Carrousel & food kiosks

VISITING TIPS (from bryantpark.org, 2026-27 season)
- The Rink is open daily from Oct 28, 2026 to Feb 28, 2027 (weather permitting), with longer hours from Nov 19 to Jan 3. Admission is free; skate rentals are paid. Reserve your skate time online, and arrive on time: ice time starts 20 minutes after your ticket time and most sessions last 50 minutes.
- Bags aren't allowed on the ice: shoe check is free, bag check is paid, and lockers are limited (bring a lock).
- Bank of America cardholders get 10% off skate rentals booked online.
- The Holiday Shops (curated by Urbanspace) are open daily from Oct 28, 2026 to Jan 3, 2027; many kiosks stay open later at peak times.
- The Tree Lighting is on Dec 1, 2026: in our film the tree isn't lit yet.
- Cozy Igloos (by ororo) are booked separately and don't include rink access.
- Evenings and weekends get very busy, as you'll see. Off-peak visits are calmer and skate rentals cost less.
- Getting there: Bryant Park sits behind the New York Public Library, between 40th and 42nd Streets and Fifth and Sixth Avenues. Subway B, D, F or M to 42 St-Bryant Park, or the 7 to 5 Av.

snippet.title: Chase Is Blocking Your AI Shopper From Using Your Card
snippet.description:
JPMorgan Chase is blocking AI agents from shopping with its customers' credit cards when customers hand the agent their card number, The Wall Street Journal reported on Nov 13, citing people familiar with the matter. Chase has not announced this itself.

The Journal says cards from Bank of America, Capital One and Citigroup are already being used by agents when customers allow it. It describes Chase as one of the more skeptical banks and says it has been slow to allow other approaches rival banks are trying, including the Visa and Mastercard agentic tokens that hide the card number and carry the shopper's spending limits.

Stripe's Link wallet gets around the block by giving the agent a one-time virtual card good for one purchase and one amount, then billing the shopper's own card. Merchants say that card costs them more to accept (WSJ, via PYMNTS).

Your AI can shop. Your bank decides if it pays.

Sources:

How does Visa make money if it never lends you a cent? Leo follows one $100 card swipe from the register to the banks: who collects the interchange fee (your bank, up to $2.40 on a premium rewards card), what Visa itself keeps (about 29 cents per $100), and who really pays for credit card rewards. Plus the 2026 fee fights: the merchant settlement, the debit-cap ruling and the DOJ lawsuit. snippet.title: Debit vs Credit Card: The Federal Fraud Trap You Must Know #shorts
snippet.description:
Using your debit card for everyday purchases could wipe out your checking account before you even notice.

Whether you bank with JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, or online banks, understanding federal card liability protections is essential to safeguarding your liquid cash.

Key Educational Takeaways:
• Under the Fair Credit Billing Act (Regulation Z), unauthorized credit card liability is capped at $50, with major card networks offering zero liability.
• Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act (Regulation E), debit card fraud drains your actual checking account cash immediately.
• If debit fraud is reported after 2 business days, statutory liability jumps to $500; after 60 calendar days from statement delivery, you can lose all stolen funds.
• Using credit cards for daily purchases, gas pumps, and online shopping keeps your primary bank deposits isolated from fraud holds.

Official Regulatory Authorities & Statutes:
• Federal Trade Commission (FTC) - Lost or Stolen Credit, ATM, and Debit Cards
• Federal Reserve Board - Regulation E (12 CFR Part 1005 - Electronic Fund Transfers)
• Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) - 12 CFR § 1026.12 (Regulation Z Special Rules for Credit Cards)

Verified Official References:
• https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/lost-or-stolen-credit-atm-debit-cards

snippet.title: The History of Bank of America | Charlotte's Bank
snippet.description: Bank of America is headquartered right here in Charlotte — but the name came from California. The Charlotte side started small: in 1960, a local bank merged with one from Greensboro to become North Carolina National Bank. A young banker named Hugh McColl took over in 1974, and he spent the next twenty years buying up banks across the South, building it into NationsBank. Then in April 1998, NationsBank bought the famous San Francisco bank, BankAmerica, for 62 billion dollars — the biggest bank deal in history at the time. Charlotte's bank was the buyer, but it took the California bank's name. That's why the biggest bank in America answers to a Charlotte address, on Tryon Street. A North Carolina bank bought the name Bank of America — and kept it. #BankOfAmerica #Charlotte #NorthCarolina #704 #QueenCity
